title: Kaempferol protects melanocytes from ferroptosis by modulating the NF-kappaB/PTGS2 signaling axis in vitiligo.
authors: Xu, Xuqing; Lei, Zixian; Hu, Wen; Wang, Hongjuan; Xiang, Fang; Ding, Yuan; Kang, Xiaojing
journal: Apoptosis : an international journal on programmed cell death
one_liner_zh: 该文研究山奈酚通过NF-kappaB/PTGS2信号轴保护黑色素细胞免于铁死亡，属于皮肤病机制与药物研究，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Oxidative stress-induced ferroptosis is increasingly recognized as an important contributor to melanocyte destruction in vitiligo; however, the specific upstream signaling networks linking inflammatory signaling to ferroptosis susceptibility remain incompletely defined. Kaempferol, a natural flavonoid and key bioactive constituent of the traditional herb Vernonia anthelmintica (L.) Willd., possesses antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, yet its potential to mitigate melanocyte ferroptosis warrants investigation. We established an RSL3 (Ras-selective lethal 3)-induced ferroptosis model in primary human melanocytes and employed a multi-dimensional approach integrating transcriptomic profiling, network pharmacology, molecular docking, and immunofluorescence analysis. Clinical relevance was validated using lesional skin tissues from vitiligo patients. RSL3 challenge triggered canonical ferroptosis features, including lethal lipid peroxidation, glutathione depletion, and characteristic mitochondrial shrinkage, all of which were significantly attenuated by kaempferol. Mechanistically, unbiased transcriptomic and network analyses identified prostaglandin-endoperoxide synthase 2 (PTGS2) as a convergent node associated with both nuclear factor-kappaB (NF-kappaB)-driven inflammatory signaling and ferroptosis stress. We found that kaempferol markedly inhibited p65 nuclear translocation, accompanied by suppression of PTGS2 transcription. Notably, pharmacological inhibition of NF-kappaB using BAY 11-7082 phenocopied the anti-ferroptosis efficacy of kaempferol, supporting the functional involvement of this signaling axis. Furthermore, clinical analyses revealed aberrant activation of the NF-kappaB/PTGS2 pathway concomitant with ferroptosis signatures in vitiligo lesions. Our findings identify ferroptosis as a critical mechanism of melanocyte injury and delineate an NF-kappaB/PTGS2-associated signaling framework linking oxidative stress, inflammatory activation, and ferroptosis damage. By modulating this stress-responsive axis, kaempferol confers robust protection against ferroptosis melanocyte injury, highlighting its potential relevance as a ferroptosis-modulating strategy.
abstract_zh: 氧化应激诱导的铁死亡（ferroptosis）日益被认为是白癜风中黑素细胞破坏的重要促成因素；然而，将炎症信号与铁死亡易感性联系起来的具体上游信号网络仍未完全明确。山奈酚（kaempferol）是一种天然黄酮类化合物，也是传统草药驱虫斑鸠菊（Vernonia anthelmintica (L.) Willd.）的关键生物活性成分，具有抗氧化和抗炎特性，但其减轻黑素细胞铁死亡的潜力尚待研究。我们在原代人黑素细胞中建立了RSL3（Ras选择性致死3）诱导的铁死亡模型，并采用整合转录组分析、网络药理学、分子对接和免疫荧光分析的多维度方法。临床相关性通过白癜风患者的皮损组织进行验证。RSL3处理触发了典型的铁死亡特征，包括致死性脂质过氧化、谷胱甘肽耗竭和特征性线粒体收缩，所有这些均被山奈酚显著减轻。机制上，无偏转录组和网络分析鉴定出前列腺素内过氧化物合酶2（PTGS2）作为与核因子-κB（NF-kappaB）驱动的炎症信号和铁死亡应激相关的汇聚节点。我们发现山奈酚显著抑制p65核转位，并伴随PTGS2转录的抑制。值得注意的是，使用BAY 11-7082对NF-kappaB的药理学抑制模拟了山奈酚的抗铁死亡功效，支持了这一信号轴的功能参与。此外，临床分析揭示白癜风皮损中NF-kappaB/PTGS2通路的异常激活与铁死亡特征并存。我们的发现将铁死亡确定为黑素细胞损伤的关键机制，并描绘了一个NF-kappaB/PTGS2相关的信号框架，将氧化应激、炎症激活和铁死亡损伤联系起来。通过调节这一应激响应轴，山奈酚赋予对铁死亡黑素细胞损伤的强效保护，凸显其作为铁死亡调节策略的潜在相关性。
